article.title: Why a Percentage Needs a Denominator
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: A percentage can sound clear even when important information is missing. Imagine a report that says, “Conversion increased by 20 percent.” Is that a large improvement? We cannot know until we understand the denominator and the original rate. If conversion rose from 1 percent to 1.2 percent, that is a 20 percent relative increase, but the absolute increase is only 0.2 percentage points. If ten people were measured, the result is also very different from a result based on one million people. Percentages always describe a relationship between a part and a whole. The whole is the denominator. When the denominator changes, the percentage can change even if the number of successful cases does not. For example, if a campaign produces 100 purchases from 10,000 eligible customers, conversion is 1 percent. If stricter eligibility rules reduce the denominator to 5,000 while the same 100 people purchase, conversion becomes 2 percent. The rate doubled, but purchases did not increase. Time period matters too. A monthly rate should not be compared casually with a yearly rate. Analysts should therefore report both the numerator and denominator when possible, together with the percentage and comparison period. It is also useful to distinguish relative change from percentage-point change. A clear sentence might say, “Conversion rose from 1.0 percent to 1.2 percent, an increase of 0.2 percentage points or 20 percent relative.” A percentage is useful, but it becomes meaningful only when we know what was counted underneath it. Analysts should state the population, denominator, observation window, and decision rule before interpreting the result. A useful review separates the observed metric from the mechanism that produced it and from the action that should follow. This makes the conclusion easier to reproduce, challenge, and communicate. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文強調，指標本身不足以支撐決策。解讀百分比、彙總結果、model drift、非顯著結果或分類 threshold 時，都必須同時確認母體、分母、比較基準、統計不確定性以及實際 business cost。只有把觀察結果與資料生成機制、決策條件分開，才能避免過度解讀。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：percentage、集計値、model drift、非有意な結果、classification thresholdは、数値だけでは意思決定を支えられない。母集団、分母、比較基準、統計的不確実性、business costを確認し、観察結果とdata generating mechanism、decision ruleを分けて解釈する必要がある。
